subject: Pricing request: Volume scenarios & proposed commit structure for BrightCart
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: hosted API rates + volume scenarios

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and prefix-caching behavior looked promising for our checkout personalization workload. Finance asked me to get a concrete rate card that shows likely monthly costs at scale so they can model FY28. We have three projected throughput scenarios for Q3: 200M tokens/mo (pilot), 1.2B tokens/mo (ramp), and 4.5B tokens/mo (run-rate).

Specifically:
- Can you provide per-token hosted API rates for committed vs. on-demand in those bands?
- Any startup/intro credits or first-quarter accelerator you typically offer?
- Do you support blended pricing for multi-month phasing (we ramp over 3 months)?

Attached is a quick forecast (BrightCart_usage_forecast.xlsx) showing month-by-month expectations and an excerpt of our SOW headcount plan. We need a ballpark by EOW so procurement can start an internal capex exercise.

Also copy procurement (procurement@brightcart.com) on any term sheets.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Head of AI Platforms
BrightCart

Attachment: BrightCart_usage_forecast.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: hosted API rates + volume scenarios

Hi Elena — great to meet you yesterday. I reviewed the forecast and that ramp looks realistic. Quick answers up front and then a suggested structure below: 

Quick summary (ballpark):
- On-demand hosted API baseline: $0.00060 / 1K input+output tokens
- Committed blended tiers (monthly commit):
  - 0–250M tokens: $0.00045 / 1K tokens (commit discount)
  - 250M–1.5B tokens: $0.00033 / 1K tokens
  - >1.5B tokens: $0.00024 / 1K tokens
- Intro accelerator: we can offer a one-time credit equal to 15% of first-month committed spend (applied as invoice credit) for new customers that sign a 12-month minimum.

Proposed structure (stacked incentives) — this is designed for phased ramps like yours:
1) Month-1 pilot: 200M tokens — offer a 3-month trial credit pool (equal to 50M tokens-worth at baseline) to make the proof-of-value cheaper.
2) Ramp months (months 2–4): commit to a staged monthly floor (you commit to 600M/mo starting month 2, increasing to 1.2B/mo by month 4). We price each month at the committed tier and apply an inter-month blending rule so you don’t overpay during the ramp.
3) Run-rate discount: once you hit sustained >=1.5B tokens/mo for two consecutive months, we move you to the top tier and convert the contract to a steady 12-month committed pricing at that level.

We usually fold in minimal legal/terms changes for standard hosted agreements; for anything that needs bespoke SLAs or private deployment we loop Legal & Solutions Engineering. I attached our internal ratecard PDF for reference (RI_ratecard_v3.pdf) — take a look and tell me which of the blended examples you want modeled.

I’ll loop Ben and Karthik on the details for approval on the intro credit and the phased blending rule. If it helps I can run three line-item scenarios and return a detailed cost table tomorrow.

Best,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_ratecard_v3.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Elena Torres <elena@brightcart.com>

Cc: BrightCart Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: hosted API rates + volume scenarios

Hi Kimberly — this looks helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups:

1) Can you model the three scenarios as: pilot month (200M), 3-month ramp (200M -> 1.2B), and 12-month annualized run-rate at 4.5B? We need an expected monthly average and annual spend for each.
2) Procurement will prefer an explicit overage mechanic: if usage exceeds committed floor in a month, we pay on-demand for the excess but would like a cap (e.g., max 1.25x of on-demand rate for bursts). Is that something you support?
3) On the intro accelerator: can you make the credit refundable against termination rather than a pure invoice credit? Our CFO wants flexibility if the project is paused.

Also, curious if Redwood supports token-based rollovers (unused committed tokens rolling forward within a 3-month window). That would help smooth seasonality for us.

If you can send a PDF with three modeled cost tables, procurement will be able to move to SOW review.

Thanks — happy to do a quick 20-min call after you send the tables.
Elena

Ben / Karthik — forwarding BrightCart’s follow-ups. Summary of asks: three modeled scenarios (pilot, ramp, run-rate); explicit overage cap request; refundable intro credit ask; token rollover for 3 months.

Suggested approach from Sales:
- Model A (conservative): apply committed tiers as I outlined. Overage priced at on-demand baseline ($0.00060/1K) with a soft cap of 1.25x only for approved burst windows (needs approval). No refundable credits, but we can apply a time-limited termination credit instead (reduces final invoice liability).
- Model B (aggressive): offer 12% deeper first-year discount if they sign a 12-month commitment (moves top-tier price to $0.00021 / 1K), and make the intro accelerator refundable up to 50% if BrightCart terminates within first 90 days. Rollover: allow up to 20% of monthly committed tokens to roll forward up to 3 months.

Approve which model we present? If we go with Model B I’ll need pre-approval on a one-time ACC credit and a legal note for the refundable clause. Also confirm if Solutions Eng needs to sign off on burst-cap safety.

Thx,
Kim

Kim — I prefer Model B but with guardrails. BrightCart is a strategic retail platform; a slightly deeper first-year discount is reasonable to win. My comments: 
- Approve the top-tier adjustment to $0.00021 / 1K for year-1 if they take a 12-month commitment and agree to an annual minimum spend (we should define a $/mo floor).
- Refundable credit: rather than refundable cash, convert to a termination credit that reduces their final payout — preserves our cash and meets their CFO halfway. If they insist on refundability, cap refund to 50% and require 60 days notice.
- Overage cap: we can commit to a 1.25x cap for planned burst windows but exclude abusive traffic (rate-limited). Solutions Eng must sign off on safety; include a usage-profile clause.
- Rollovers: allow up to 15% monthly rollover within a 3-month window.

If you present Model B with these guardrails I’m comfortable. Loop Legal for the exact clause language; I’ll flag this with Revenue Ops for deal accounting.

Ben
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposal: BrightCart hosted API pricing (model B w/guardrails)

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise proposal PDF with three modeled cost tables per your request and a draft term sheet (BrightCart_term_sheet_draft.docx). Summary of the proposed commercial: 

1) Pricing (hosted API, input+output tokens):
   - Baseline on-demand: $0.00060 / 1K tokens
   - Committed tiers (monthly committed tokens):
     * 0–250M: $0.00045 / 1K
     * 250M–1.5B: $0.00033 / 1K
     * >1.5B: $0.00021 / 1K (year-1 promotional top tier under Model B)
2) Intro accelerator: one-time credit equivalent to 15% of first-month committed spend. This will be issued as a termination-credit instrument (reduces final invoice liability). Refundable cash only if BrightCart requests cash refund and agrees to a 60-day notice window (refund capped at 50% of the credit).
3) Overage mechanics: over-commit usage billed at on-demand rate ($0.00060 / 1K) with a negotiated burst cap of up to 1.25x on-demand for approved burst windows. Abusive or sustained overages excluded; see usage profile appendix.
4) Rollovers: up to 15% of committed monthly tokens may roll forward for up to 3 months.
5) Transition to run-rate: after two consecutive months >=1.5B tokens, account moves to steady 12-month committed top tier pricing.

Next steps: I’ve left placeholders in the term sheet for annual minimum and approved burst window dates. If this looks acceptable I’ll ask Legal to produce a formal SOW and send a DocuSign for signatures. We can also set a quick 20-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the cost tables.

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
